title: Reinforcing VLAs in Task-Agnostic World Models
claim: Prior pipelines tie world and reward models to specific tasks and data; ours decouples them into task-agnostic components that generalize zero-shot.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, left prior vs right ours, color-coded task-specific vs task-agnostic
description: A two-panel comparison with a title above each panel. The left panel, 'Previous: In-Domain Only World Model', has a pink background. It flows left to right: a robot image for a target task, grids of target rollout collection frames, a brace grouping a task-specific world model (grey globe) and a task-specific reward model (graph icon), then an 'RL in WM' box. A bottom strip lists three drawbacks: massive in-domain data, tied to seen tasks, and no unseen generalization (black X). The right panel, 'Our Paradigm: General-Purpose World Model', mixes blue task-agnostic regions with pink task-specific regions. Untargeted behavior frames feed a blue-globe task-agnostic world model. New tasks then branch into several few-shot SFT scenes, each with its own 'RL in WM' box, and a task-agnostic VLM reward model. A bottom strip lists the benefits, ending in a green check mark. A legend at the bottom maps pink to task-specific and blue to task-agnostic.
caption: Left: Previous WM-based RL pipelines for VLA post-training tightly couple the WM and reward models to known target tasks, requiring thousands of in-domain rollouts, precluding unseen adaptation. Right: RAW-Dream decouples dynamics learning from task semantics. A general-purpose WM pre-trained on diverse task-free behaviors captures transferable physical priors, while a foundation VLM provides zero-shot rewards. Together, they enable data-efficient RL on novel tasks.
abstract: Post-training Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models via reinforcement learning (RL) in learned world models has emerged as an effective strategy to adapt to new tasks without costly real-world interactions. However, while using imagined trajectories reduces the sample complexity of policy training, existing methods still heavily rely on task-specific data to fine-tune both the world and reward models, fundamentally limiting their scalability to unseen tasks. To overcome this, we argue that world and reward models should capture transferable physical priors that enable zero-shot inference. We propose RAW-Dream (Reinforcing VLAs in task-Agnostic World Dreams), a new paradigm that completely disentangles world model learning from downstream task dependencies. RAW-Dream utilizes a world model pre-trained on diverse task-free behaviors for predicting future rollouts, and an off-the-shelf Vision-Language Model (VLM) for reward generation. Because both components are task-agnostic, VLAs can be readily finetuned for any new task entirely within this zero-shot imagination. Furthermore, to mitigate world model hallucinations, we introduce a dual-noise verification mechanism to filter out unreliable rollouts. Extensive experiments across simulation and real-world settings demonstrate consistent performance gains, proving that generalized physical priors can effectively substitute for costly task-dependent data, offering a highly scalable roadmap for VLA adaptation.
